subject: Media Literacy
title: International Perspectives on Bias
description: A short lesson to help you apply International Perspectives on Bias.

hook.text: American media shows Israel-Palestine one way. Arab media shows it another. Same events. Opposite narratives.

buildup.text: Media bias varies dramatically by country, shaped by national interests, cultural values, and press freedom.

discovery.text: Reading international coverage of the same event reveals biases invisible from within any single country's media.

twist.text: Your country's media bias is invisible to you because you're immersed in it. Outsiders see it immediately.

climax.text: Consuming international news is one of the most effective ways to recognize your own media's blind spots.

punchline.text: Read foreign news about your country. You'll see yourself differently.

quiz.question: Why is reading international news coverage valuable?
options: Foreign media is always less biased
It reveals biases in your own country's media that are invisible from within
